links.outcome: Hallucination rate of EHR-embedded generative AI summaries, measured at atomic content unit level
links.effect: Hallucination rate 11.79% (95% CI, 11.47% to 12.10%) across 671 summaries containing 40,452 ACUs; the detector agreed with physician adjudication on 96.95% of ACUs in the validation set.
links.quote: Across 671 remaining summaries containing 40,452 ACUs, the hallucination rate was 11.79% (95% CI, 11.47% to 12.10%).

links.outcome: Reproducibility of regenerated summaries (textual and semantic similarity) across repeated runs
links.effect: Among 385 regenerated pairs, 32.7% were textually identical and 37.9% were semantically identical.
links.quote: Among 385 regenerated pairs of summaries, 32.7% were textually identical and 37.9% were semantically identical.

unlisted_practices: Agentic hallucination detector that decomposes summaries into atomic content units and verifies each against source notes
Measuring source note utilization by generative summarizers (mean 5.8% of available notes used)

screen.practice: Multidimensional post-deployment assurance monitoring (hallucination detection, consistency checks, clinician feedback)
screen.reason: Evaluates a real-world deployed EHR generative AI summarization tool across seven hospitals using a multidimensional assurance framework and validates an agentic hallucination detector to audit deployment safety and consistency.

primary.practice: agentic hallucination detection / post-deployment assurance auditing
